Building Custom Behaviors

A custom Behavior is a user-authored pipeline extension that plugs into a stage in the pipeline. Custom Behaviors follow the same contract and lifecycle as built-in Behaviors, allowing engineers to add domain-specific logic to any supported pipeline stage without modifying internals. Because custom Behaviors are subject to the same stage isolation, ordering, and lifecycle rules as built-in Behaviors, they extend pipeline capabilities without compromising its deterministic execution guarantees.

Every Behavior—built-in or custom—implements BehaviorContract<T> and is decorated with @VaultBehavior. The orchestrator discovers, validates, and executes custom Behaviors exactly as it does core Behaviors.

What You Need

A complete custom Behavior consists of the following pieces:

  1. A Behavior class decorated with @VaultBehavior and implementing BehaviorContract<T>.
  2. An options interface that defines the configuration the Behavior accepts.
  3. A fluent API installer (installFluentApi) so engineers can configure the Behavior with a chained method call on the FeatureCell.
  4. An optional extension interface with TypeScript module augmentation if the Behavior adds new methods to the FeatureCell API surface.
  5. Registration in the FeatureCell declaration's Behavior array.
Step 1 — Define an Options Interface

The options interface describes the configuration your Behavior expects. It is passed to the constructor via behaviorCtx.behaviorConfig. 

{{`export interface MyBehaviorOptions<T> {
  /** How often the Behavior runs its check, in milliseconds. */
  intervalMs: number;

  /** Optional predicate to skip processing for certain values. */
  shouldSkip?: (value: T) => boolean;
}`}}
Step 2 — Create the Behavior Class

Decorate the class with @VaultBehavior and implement BehaviorContract<T>. The decorator metadata tells the orchestrator which pipeline stage to assign the Behavior to, its unique key, and whether it requires configuration. 

{{`import {
  BehaviorClassContext,
  BehaviorContract,
  BehaviorType,
  BehaviorTypes,
  defineBehaviorKey,
  FeatureCellBaseShape,
  FeatureCellExtensionContext,
  VaultBehavior
} from '@sdux-vault/shared';

import { MyBehaviorOptions } from './my-behavior.options';

@VaultBehavior({
  type: BehaviorTypes.Extension,
  key: defineBehaviorKey('Custom', 'MyBehavior'),
  critical: false,
  wantsConfig: true,
  configKey: 'withMyBehavior'
})
export class withMyBehavior<T> implements BehaviorContract<T> {

  // ── Static metadata (mirrored by the decorator) ──────────
  static readonly type: BehaviorType;
  static readonly key: string;
  static readonly critical: boolean;
  static readonly wantsConfig: boolean;
  static readonly configKey: string;

  // ── Instance fields ──────────────────────────────────────
  readonly type = withMyBehavior.type;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly critical = withMyBehavior.critical;

  readonly #options: MyBehaviorOptions<T>;

  // ── Fluent API installer ─────────────────────────────────
  static installFluentApi<T>(
    cell: FeatureCellBaseShape<T>,
    behaviorConfigs: Map<string, unknown>
  ) {
    cell.withMyBehavior = function (options: MyBehaviorOptions<T>) {
      behaviorConfigs.set(withMyBehavior.configKey, options);
      return this;
    };
  }

  // ── Constructor ──────────────────────────────────────────
  constructor(key: string, readonly behaviorCtx: BehaviorClassContext) {
    this.key = key;
    this.#options = behaviorCtx.behaviorConfig as MyBehaviorOptions<T>;

    if (typeof this.#options?.intervalMs !== 'number') {
      throw new Error(
        '[vault] withMyBehavior requires intervalMs (number).'
      );
    }
  }

  // ── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────
  extendCellAPI(ctx: FeatureCellExtensionContext<T>): void {
    // Subscribe to state emissions, set up timers, etc.
  }

  reset(): void {
    // Reset internal state between pipeline cycles.
  }

  destroy(): void {
    // Tear down subscriptions and release resources.
  }
}`}}
Note

The static fields (type, key, critical, wantsConfig, configKey) are populated at runtime by the @VaultBehavior decorator. Declare them as static readonly for type safety.

Decorator Metadata Reference

The @VaultBehavior decorator accepts the following metadata:

BehaviorMetaShape
Property Description
type: BehaviorType

required

 The pipeline stage in which this Behavior participates. Determines when the orchestrator invokes the Behavior. Use a value from BehaviorTypes.
key: string

required

 Unique identifier for this Behavior. Created with defineBehaviorKey('Domain', 'Name'). The key follows the format SDUX::Behavior::Domain::Name. Used for diagnostics, DevTools visualization, and orchestrator classification.
critical: boolean

required

 Indicates whether this Behavior is critical. When true, any error in this Behavior halts the pipeline. When false, errors are logged and the pipeline continues.
resolveType?: ResolveType

optional

 Optional resolve strategy associated with this Behavior. Only set for resolution Behaviors that determine how state is initially derived (e.g., value, http, observable).
wantsConfig?: boolean

optional

 When true, the orchestrator passes the fluent configuration to the constructor via behaviorCtx.behaviorConfig.
configKey?: string

optional

 The key used to look up the Behavior's configuration from the fluent API config map.
needsLicense?: boolean

optional

 Indicates whether this Behavior requires a valid license to execute. When true, the orchestrator validates the license before invoking the Behavior.
licenseId?: string

optional

 The license identifier required for this Behavior. Used by the orchestrator to validate that the appropriate license is present.
Step 3 — Module Augmentation (Optional)

If your Behavior adds new methods to the FeatureCell (via extendCellAPI), declare them using TypeScript module augmentation so consumers get full type safety. 

{{`import { MyBehaviorOptions } from '../options/my-behavior.options';

export interface MyBehaviorExtension<T> {
  myCustomMethod(arg: string): Promise<T>;
}

declare module '@sdux-vault/shared' {
  interface FeatureCellExtension<T> {
    myCustomMethod?(arg: string): Promise<T>;
  }

  interface FeatureCellFluentApi<T> {
    withMyBehavior?(options: MyBehaviorOptions<T>): this;
  }
}`}}

This augmentation makes cell.myCustomMethod() and cell.withMyBehavior() available with full IntelliSense in consuming code.

Step 4 — Register the Behavior

Pass the Behavior class to the FeatureCell declaration's Behavior array. Then use the fluent API to provide configuration. 

{{`import { FeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/core';
import { withMyBehavior } from './with-my-behavior.behavior';

export const myCell = FeatureCell(
  MyCellToken,
  {
    key: 'my-cell',
    initialState: {}
  },
  [
    withMyBehavior   // register in the behavior array
  ],
  []
);

myCell
  .withMyBehavior({ intervalMs: 5000 })
  .initialize();`}}
Behavior Lifecycle

The orchestrator manages each Behavior through a predictable lifecycle:

  1. Construction — The orchestrator instantiates the Behavior, passing the assigned key and a context object containing the configuration (if wantsConfig is true).
  2. extendCellAPI — Called once after construction if the Behavior exposes extension methods on the FeatureCell.
  3. Pipeline execution — The Behavior's stage-specific logic runs each time the pipeline processes a state change.
  4. reset — Called when the pipeline resets between cycles. Use this to clear caches or internal counters.
  5. destroy — Called when the FeatureCell is destroyed. Tear down all subscriptions and release resources.
Extending an Existing Behavior

You can extend a built-in Behavior class to inherit its base logic and override or augment specific methods. This is useful when you need the same pipeline stage assignment and core mechanics but want to customize a subset of the logic. 

{{`import {
  BehaviorTypes,
  defineBehaviorKey,
  VaultBehavior
} from '@sdux-vault/shared';
import { withDistinctUntilChangedBehavior } from '@sdux-vault/addons';

@VaultBehavior({
  type: BehaviorTypes.Operator,
  key: defineBehaviorKey('Custom', 'CustomDistinct'),
  critical: false,
  wantsConfig: true,
  configKey: 'withCustomDistinct'
})
export class withCustomDistinctBehavior<T>
  extends withDistinctUntilChangedBehavior<T> {

  // Override or add methods as needed.
  // The parent class handles the standard distinct logic.
  // Your subclass can customize the comparison function,
  // add logging, or inject additional side effects.
}`}}
Note

When extending an existing Behavior, apply a new @VaultBehavior decorator with a unique key and configKey. The new decorator replaces the parent's metadata so the orchestrator treats your subclass as a distinct Behavior.

Abstract Behavior Base Classes

provides abstract base classes for Behavior categories that share significant implementation logic. The StepwiseBehaviorAbstract<T> class, for example, encapsulates the coordination protocol with the stepwise controller bus. Concrete implementations such as withStepwiseResolveBehavior, withStepwiseFilterBehavior, and withStepwiseReducerBehavior each extend this abstract base.

When building a family of related Behaviors, consider extracting shared logic into an abstract class. This avoids duplication while preserving the single-responsibility contract that each concrete Behavior must satisfy.

For most custom Behaviors that target a single pipeline stage, implementing BehaviorContract<T> directly is the recommended approach. Use an abstract base only when you are creating multiple Behaviors that share substantial internal mechanics.

Extensible Behavior Types

The following Behavior types are available for custom Extensions. Each type corresponds to a pipeline stage where the custom Behavior will execute.

Extensible Behavior Types
Behavior Type Description
Encrypt Behaviors that apply encryption or decryption transformations to state values during pipeline processing. The developer assumes complete responsibility for protecting the end-user's data.
ErrorTransform Behaviors that transform or enrich error objects before they are dispatched to error callbacks.
Extension General-purpose Behaviors that add methods to the FeatureCell API surface.
Interceptor Behaviors that observe or react to pipeline events such as errors.
Merge Behaviors that define custom merge strategies for combining current and incoming state.
Operator Behaviors that apply RxJS operators to the emission stream.
Persist Behaviors that persist committed state to external storage such as localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB. The developer assumes complete responsibility for protecting the end-user's data.
ReplayGlobalError Behaviors that replay previously captured global errors into the pipeline for reprocessing or observation.
StepwiseFilter Behaviors that conditionally suppress pipeline values using the stepwise bus coordination protocol.
StepwiseReducer Behaviors that derive or transform candidate values using the stepwise bus coordination protocol.
StepwiseResolve Behaviors that normalize incoming state inputs using the stepwise bus coordination protocol.
Restricted Behavior Types

Not all Behavior types are available for custom Extensions. The Orchestrator enforces a strict boundary between core pipeline infrastructure and the extensible Behavior surface. Behaviors that belong to core pipeline stages are managed exclusively by the Orchestrator and are silently removed if provided in the FeatureCell Behavior array.

The following Behavior types are restricted and cannot be registered as custom Extensions:

Restricted Behavior Types
Behavior Type Reason
CoreAfterTap Executes registered AfterTap observation callbacks. Managed internally by the Orchestrator.
CoreBeforeTap Executes registered BeforeTap observation callbacks. Managed internally by the Orchestrator.
CoreEmitState Dispatches finalized State to registered emit-state callbacks. Managed internally based on FeatureCell emit-state callback configuration.
CoreError Normalizes raw errors into the canonical error shape. Exactly one instance is required and is provided by the core pipeline.
CoreErrorCallback Dispatches normalized errors to registered error callbacks. Managed internally based on FeatureCell error callback configuration.
CoreState Manages finalized State commitment and snapshot emission. Exactly one instance is required and is provided by the core pipeline.
Filter Applies registered filter functions to pipeline values. The core Filter Behavior is provided by the pipeline; filter functions are supplied separately through FeatureCell configuration.
FromObservable Resolves Observable-based State inputs. Installed as part of the core Resolve stage.
FromPromise Resolves deferred factory (Promise-backed) State inputs. Installed as part of the core Resolve stage.
FromStream Resolves stream-based State inputs. Installed as part of the core Resolve stage.
Reduce Applies registered reducer functions to pipeline values. The core Reduce Behavior is provided by the pipeline; reducer functions are supplied separately through FeatureCell configuration.
Resolve Normalizes incoming State inputs into a canonical upstream value. Core Resolve Behaviors are installed by default and execute based on the resolved input type.

If a custom Behavior is registered with any of the restricted types listed above, the Orchestrator removes it during pipeline initialization. No error is raised; the Behavior is silently excluded from pipeline execution.

Licensing

Custom Behavior extensions are available exclusively with a purchased Pro plan. The licensing controller validates the active license during pipeline initialization and silently excludes custom Behaviors when a valid Pro license is not present. For licensing details and plan options, see the product page.
